name: Farcinema
tagline: See the unseen cinema of the Middle East
description: Farcinema is an independent film curation program in the San Francisco Bay Area. We show new Middle Eastern films that win at Cannes, Berlinale, Venice, Sundance, and Tribeca and then rarely get a release here.

series.title: Let Her Sing 2026: Film Screenings
series.subtitle: Women, Music & the Freedom to Sing

venue.name: Yerba Buena Center for the Arts

tickets.label: Get tickets
tickets.note: Sold per film, or as a pass for the whole day.

intro: For the 10th anniversary of Let Her Sing: A Celebration of Female Voices, Diaspora Arts Connection and Farcinema present a day of three films at YBCA in San Francisco. All three are about women who keep singing when they are told to stop.

No Land's Song, A Sister's Tale, and Sonita move between Afghanistan, the Middle East, Europe, and the diaspora. In each of them, a woman's voice is the thing at stake. After the last film, Gelareh Sheibani and Yara Daneshvar join us for a conversation and audience questions.
series.closing: Tickets are sold per film, or as a pass for the whole day. Come for one, or stay from eleven to five.

films.title: No Land's Song
synopsis: Middle Eastern composer Sara Najafi sets out to accomplish something that has become extraordinarily difficult in the Middle East: organize a public concert featuring women singing solo. Determined to revive a musical tradition pushed from public life, she brings together Middle Eastern and French women musicians for a concert in Tehran.

Director Ayat Najafi follows the project over more than two years as Sara navigates government bureaucracy, censorship, cultural restrictions, and uncertainty over whether the performance will ever be permitted to take place. Part musical journey and part chronicle of resistance, it asks what happens when a society restricts the female voice.

films.title: A Sister's Tale
synopsis: Filmed over seven years, A Sister's Tale is director Leila Amini's deeply personal portrait of her sister, Nasreen, a mother of two living in Tehran who begins to reclaim a dream she had long put aside: becoming a singer.

After years devoted to marriage and family, Nasreen becomes determined to pursue music despite opposition within her marriage and the restrictions placed on women singing publicly in the Middle East. What begins as the story of one woman finding her voice becomes a moving examination of family, marriage, motherhood, and female self-determination.

films.title: Sonita
synopsis: Sonita follows a spirited young Afghan refugee living in Tehran who dreams of becoming a rapper. While she writes songs inspired by artists she admires and imagines a future in music, her family has other plans: they intend to marry her off in exchange for money.

Living in a country where women face restrictions on singing publicly, Sonita turns to rap as a way to tell her own story and challenge the forces trying to determine her future. At once intimate and urgent, it is a portrait of a young woman discovering that her voice can become one of her most powerful tools for freedom.
